note: Project-local source inventory. The repository root evidence policy remains controlling; source class and operational states are separate. For a historical source served through a modern digital presentation, evidenceClass describes the underlying source when stated, while accessState and rightsState describe what is actually accessed and can be reused.

sources.title: Uyt-spanningen — first-edition text (1676)
sources.type: Digital, explicitly diplomatic presentation of the 1676 source edition
supports: Title-page imprint, original collection and primary text witness
limits: DBNL marks the underlying 1676 work Auteursrechtvrij, but the online transcription is diplomatic rather than a complete unmediated scan; its colophon records omissions and editorial corrections. Use the exact page or scan for poem-level claims.

sources.title: DBNL colophon for the 1676 Uyt-spanningen transcription
sources.type: Editorial record about the digital transcription and its corrections
supports: Transcription method, the omitted material, editorial corrections, and the explicit 1664→1674 emendation of the Rees poem date
limits: This is modern editorial documentation, not the original printing itself; it identifies a correction but does not replace visual inspection of the 1676 leaf.

sources.title: Uyt-spanningen — critical edition and apparatus (2005)
sources.type: Critical edition edited by A. Ros and L. Strengholt
supports: Modern item numbering, critical text, variants, notes, tune directions, bibliography and literary-historical framing
limits: DBNL explicitly marks this edition as copyrighted. Item numbers may group multiple original texts; some repetitions/stanzas are editorially supplied for melody. Do not reproduce its full text or apparatus without permission.

sources.title: Schepselen niet en Jesus al — critical-edition item 51
sources.type: Exact critical-edition page for title, tune direction and date
supports: Title spelling, tune direction Singt als: Rosemont waer gy vliedt, stanza organization, and November 1661 date shown by the critical edition
limits: This is the 2005 copyrighted critical text, not the original 1676 leaf; exact transcription/quotation must be checked against the original edition for quote-sensitive claims.

sources.title: Christen sangers — preface in the critical edition
sources.type: Critical-edition transcription of Lodenstein's preface on song
supports: Lodenstein's reflections on poetry, music and the heart
limits: A modern paraphrase must not be presented as a verbatim quotation; the accessed edition is copyrighted.

sources.title: Niet en al, Dat is: Des werelds ydelheyd en Gods Al-genoegsaamheyd
sources.type: Exact text page in the 1676 first-edition digital transcription
supports: Original-print title, long refrain-based text, and source text for a future candidate
limits: The text is lengthy and internally sectioned. Count stanzas/sections and evaluate whether to adapt all or a defined portion before choosing a SUNO duration.

sources.title: De Algenoegsaamheyd Of Aandagt op Ps. 73:25 en Luc. 10:42
sources.type: Exact text page in the 1676 first-edition digital transcription
supports: Original-print title and its explicit biblical references to Psalm 73:25 and Luke 10:42
limits: Classify the text's genre and melodic status from the full page before treating it as a singable hymn.

sources.title: Jesus Lijdende Liefde
sources.type: Exact text page in the 1676 first-edition digital transcription
supports: Original title and printed tune direction Ten is niet alle tijd, &c.
limits: Historical tune direction does not prove that a future modern SUNO setting reproduces the historical performance.

sources.title: Nieuw-Jaars Gebedt, Om Lust tot en in Gods Woord
sources.type: Exact text page in the 1676 first-edition digital transcription
supports: Original title and printed tune direction Chermets secrets; a recurring refrain is visible in the text
limits: Verify all stanzas and refrain placement in the complete source before preparing a lyric adaptation.

sources.title: Den nedrigen christen, Op Psalm 131
sources.type: Exact text page in the 1676 first-edition digital transcription
supports: Original title, Psalm 131 anchor and tune direction Prendete la (as transcribed in the source page)
limits: Check the historical spelling, stanza/refrain structure and melodic identification against the original image before publication.

sources.title: Toe-Sang Der Gelovigen in het Vaderland — voyage-related song
sources.type: Exact text page in the 1676 first-edition digital transcription
supports: Original title and tune direction Stemme: Ps. CIII; related to the voyage-song material about travel to the East Indies
limits: Verify the companion song and exact narrative context from the preceding source pages before treating this as an independent standalone song.

sources.title: I. Hert-sterckte in Jehova, Op 1 Sam. 30:6 — critical-edition item 34
sources.type: Critical-edition page for the first Rees song
supports: The distinction between I and II, the date 28 December 1673 shown by the critical edition, and its own melody directions Onherroepelijke Jeugd or Gavotte. A la fronté
limits: The critical edition is copyrighted. This is not the source poem used for the later Rutgers hymn no. 68; do not conflate it with the second Hert-sterckte.

sources.title: II. Hert-sterckte in Jehova — selected text in a 1971 anthology
sources.type: Later anthology / bloemlezing presenting the second Rees song
supports: The second poem's text and the date printed in the digital presentation as 4 January 1674
limits: The accompanying note states that the original had an erroneous 1664; the DBNL colophon also records an editorial 1664→1674 correction. Keep the date claim on EVIDENCE_HOLD until the original page image is checked.
The date claim is specifically held in CLM-HERT-II-DATE-1674 until an original page image is checked; other textual claims from this page must be assessed individually.

sources.title: Rees songs — historical context
sources.type: Contextual page associated with the selected Rees songs
supports: Context for the sequence of consolatory songs composed during the Rees hostage period
limits: Do not treat the contextual page as proof of every detail of the hostage narrative without further primary corroboration.

sources.title: Evangelische Gezangen (1806), hymn LXVIII: Zelfverloochening
sources.type: Exact historical hymnbook item in the 1806 collection
supports: Hymn number, title, seven-stanza form and the text used as the basis for the later Russian adaptation
limits: This is the Rutgers-reworked hymnbook version, not a verbatim transcription of the full 1674 Lodenstein poem. DBNL identifies the underlying 1806 book as public-domain; check terms for the digital representation separately.

sources.title: Evangelische Gezangen — collection-level record (1806)
sources.type: Collection-level digital presentation of the original 1806 hymnbook
supports: Collection context and the place of hymn LXVIII in the book
limits: Use the individual hymn page for the exact text; do not infer that every later melody association was part of the 1806 source.

sources.title: Abraham Rutgers — historical biographical dictionary entry
sources.type: Historical biographical dictionary article
supports: Rutgers's editorial roles and the attribution of hymnbook items 68 and 62 to Lodenstein material revised by Rutgers
limits: Secondary source. Collate the editions if exact stanza-by-stanza editorial changes are to be claimed.

sources.title: Afrikaans Lied 276 — modern source-chain page
sources.type: Modern institutional song page with an adaptation chain
supports: The listed chain from Lodenstein and Rutgers through Gerdener (1931), Pienaar / AGB (1944), Van der Merwe (1978), and Breytenbach (2001); current melody association
limits: This is secondary chain evidence, not the physical witness for each intermediary edition. Modern Afrikaans lyrics and recordings have separate rights. The melody associated with the modern song must not be attributed as Lodenstein's original tune without a primary witness.

sources.title: Afrikaans Lied 271 — modern source-chain page
sources.type: Modern institutional song page
supports: Discovery of another Lodenstein-derived Afrikaans text and its reported edition chain
limits: Exact original Dutch title and each intermediate text version remain to be checked.

sources.title: Jacobus Revius — author bibliography
sources.type: Bibliographic / biographical author record
supports: Name variant Jacob Reefsen, life dates, and records for the 1630 collection, 1621 Song of Songs work and 1640 revised metrical Psalter
limits: Bibliographic record is not a full primary witness and does not by itself identify a composition date for every poem.

sources.title: Over-Ysselsche sangen en dichten — scholarly edition contents
sources.type: Contents / entrypoint for W.A.P. Smit's 1930–1935 scholarly edition
supports: Collection structure, edition identification and discovery of the sonnet
limits: This is not a direct scan of the 1630 leaf. The modern scholarly edition has a separate rights layer.

sources.title: Hy droech onse smerten — poem page in the W.A.P. Smit edition
sources.type: Exact page for the sonnet in the 1930–1935 scholarly edition
supports: Fourteen-line sonnet, textual sequence and editorial glosses
limits: Do not describe this page as a facsimile of the 1630 edition; no original tune direction has been verified.

sources.title: J.F. Geerds, critical discussion of Hy droech onse smerten (1976)
sources.type: Specialist secondary study
supports: Close-reading interpretation of the poem's turn and movement from 'our' to 'my' sins
limits: Use the text witness for quotations; this study supports interpretation, not first-publication or musical attribution by itself.

sources.title: Over-Ysselsche sangen en dichten — 1630 edition as underlying work
sources.type: Bibliographic lead to the original 1630 edition; original leaf not independently acquired in this project
supports: Existence of the historical edition as a primary bibliographic target
limits: The author bibliography is a discovery lead, not the original 1630 object. Treat composition date, original punctuation and physical edition facts as unverified until the first-edition witness is acquired.

sources.title: Church Order associated with Dordrecht, Article 69
sources.type: Online presentation of a historical church-order provision
supports: Prescribed public-worship repertoire and the restriction of other songs in the relevant church-order text
limits: The webpage is a mediated transcription; confirm edition provenance before quoting exact legal wording. A normative rule does not prove uniform actual use in every congregation.

sources.title: Earlier Dutch Reformed synodical church-order text (1578)
sources.type: Online presentation of an earlier historical church-order provision
supports: Prehistory of psalm-first church-song regulations and the Datheen psalm tradition
limits: This page is a mediated transcription; quote the particular year's text rather than blend several synods into a single rule.

sources.title: Hymni ofte Loff-sangen — 1967 facsimile of a work first printed in 1615
sources.type: Digital presentation of the 1967 facsimile edition edited by Jan van Biezen and Marie Veldhuyzen
supports: The accessed item's edition date, editors, reproduction notes, the original work's 1615 date, and the preface's Ephesians 5:19 rationale
limits: This is a copyrighted 1967 facsimile, not an independently digitized 1615 original. DBNL notes omissions and editorial changes in the digital rendering.

sources.title: Hymni ofte Loff-sangen — underlying 1615 original work
sources.type: Original 1615 work represented through the 1967 facsimile; original not independently acquired here
supports: Original title and the portions of 1615 front matter reproduced in the facsimile
limits: The accessible evidence is mediated by the 1967 edition; the right to reproduce the facsimile or its modern editorial matter is separate from the public-domain age of the underlying work.

sources.title: Louis Peter Grijp — musicological context for Dutch song and melody reuse
sources.type: Musicological secondary study
supports: Historical context for tune reuse / contrafactum and the Rosemont melody
limits: Use the poem's own tune direction for song-specific claims; secondary musicology cannot prove that a modern generated setting reproduces the original sound.
